messages:
incident-bot: PagerDuty P1 — Elevated 5xx/timeouts observed for tenant 'springfield-prod' on Dedicated cluster dc-east-1. Start 2026-03-14T11:34:xxZ. Current symptom: ~40% 5xx, many tcp timeouts. Pager: oncall-sre. Alert links: https://pd.example/pd/incidents/INC12345

oncall-sre: Ack, I'm on it. Taking ownership.

maria (SRE): Joining. Looking at node metrics: gpu-node-07 and gpu-node-09 show heavy GPU mem churn and kernel OOM logs. 95th latency up to 3.9s. Patterns look like capacity exhaustion/noisy neighbor from tenant springfield-prod.

dan (infra): I see repeated pod evictions and GpuOOM events on gpu-node-07:
```
Mar 14 11:36:12 gpu-node-07 kubelet: Evicting pod springfield-prod-backfill-2 (reason: GpuOutOfMemory)
Mar 14 11:36:15 kernel: Out of memory: Kill process 4521 (python) total-vm:12000000kB, anon-rss:10500000kB
```
These backfills started at 11:29 after a customer scheduled a large job.

jess (eng-platform): Can we throttle the tenant quickly and/or move them to a burst pool? Propose: apply per-tenant concurrency cap to 10, and scale dedicated-pool-east +1 as temporary relief.

oncall-sre: Applying concurrency cap now via internal routing API. Command: 
```bash
curl -X POST "https://internal-api.redwood/api/v1/routing/tenants/springfield-prod/cap" -d '{"concurrency":10}' -H 'Authorization: Bearer REDACTED'
```

deploy-bot: routing-change | rr-842 | applied by oncall-sre at 2026-03-14T11:46:03Z | change-id:chg-9981

maria (SRE): After applying the cap error rate dropped from 40% -> ~12% but still elevated. Some nodes still show GPU memory pressure and throttled jobs. I traced traffic — there is a long-running KV cache priming job `springfield-backfill-2` that spikes memory for minutes.

dan (infra): I'll cordon gpu-node-07 and drain the noisy pods to free up memory. Doing a graceful evict to avoid OOM kills.

alex (customer-success): Reaching out to Springfield SRE: "We're throttling concurrency and may migrate some batch workloads momentarily. We'll keep you posted." @sam FYI.

sam (account-exec): Please add a short customer note template and include expected timeline (30–60m). I'll handle follow-up.

jess (eng-platform): Also enabling fallback routing for this tenant to a smaller model variant to reduce per-request memory (redwood-small-quant). That should reduce pressure by ~50–60%.

oncall-sre: Enabling fallback now via routing rules. API call: 
```bash
curl -X POST "https://internal-api.redwood/api/v1/tenant-routing" -d '{"tenant":"springfield-prod","fallback_model":"redwood-small-quant"}'
```

deploy-bot: model-fallback | tenant=springfield-prod | redwood-small-quant | applied at 2026-03-14T11:49:21Z

maria (SRE): Confirming: after fallback + eviction + concurrency cap, 5xx down to ~1.5%, latency back to baseline. Node memory pressure normalized. Keeping elevated monitoring for 10m.

oncall-sre: Incident mitigated — switching to monitored state. Will keep thread open for postmortem and follow-ups.

incident-bot: PagerDuty: Incident INC12345 transitioned to MITIGATED by oncall-sre. Start=1769154321, Mitigated=1769154699, duration=578s. Please file postmortem and assign owners.

alex (customer-success): Customer notified. They acknowledged the mitigation and will postpone the large backfill. They requested guidance on job sizing.

oncall-sre: Action items captured: 1) Postmortem (owners: maria, jess). 2) Automate per-tenant caps on Dedicated clusters. 3) Improve detection of long-running KV priming/backfills. 4) Add an automatic fallback policy for model-size when memory pressure detected. I'll create JIRA tickets and link.

sam (account-exec): Thanks team — solid quick coordination. Please include customer timeline and recommended guardrails in the postmortem. :thumbsup:

jess (eng-platform): I'll draft a runbook change and add a step to escalate to account execs when we apply throttles/migrations.

oncall-sre: Closing notes: root cause = tenant scheduled large concurrent backfill that saturated GPU memory on a small Dedicated pool node -> noisy neighbor evictions. Short-term mitigations: concurrency cap, drain noisy pods, fallback to smaller model, scale pool. Long-term: quota enforcement + automation.

sam (account-exec): Great work everyone. :tada:
